title: Canonical finite derived pullback tensor comparison
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1}$ for $n\geq0$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be any scheme morphism on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the finite derived pullback and tensor functors of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Define their canonical comparison $\mu_{f,n}:L f_n^*(M\otimes^L N)\simeq L f_n^*M\otimes^L L f_n^*N$ for arbitrary ambient derived objects $M,N$ by totalizing the ordinary module pullback/tensor isomorphism on flat-term K-flat representatives, descending to the derived category, and conjugating by the specified intrinsic realization and tensor-model isomorphisms. It is the actual map characterized by this representative square. Define the derived Koszul symmetry by descent of the signed cochain exchange $x_p\otimes y_q\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y_q\otimes x_p$. Include the four pullback/tensor comparison-family types for the coefficient categories and operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. These constructions introduce no alternative derived tensor or pullback functor. The canonical finite family satisfies the naturality, associativity, signed symmetry, both unit and pullback-composition equations with the recorded canonical operation comparisons.

source.place: Lemma 21.18.4 (Tag 07A4, label lemma-pullback-tensor-product), for the morphism of ringed topoi (X_proet, (A_{E,n})_X) -> (Y_proet, (A_{E,n})_Y); the integral, rational and Qlbar levels follow the level-by-level definitions of the operations in def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom

proof.text: For pullbackTensorIndependent use the first property of the given flat-term K-flat representative: at these universes the two K-flat predicates are definitionally equal.

For pullbackTensorFiniteRepresentative_existsUnique use ObjectProperty.ιOfLE to include flat-term K-flat complexes among all K-flat complexes, and whisker T.comparison with the product inclusion. Set the tensor field to S.tensor. The component equation is reflexive. For uniqueness eliminate the asserted tensor-functor equality, then use isomorphism and natural-transformation extensionality and the prescribed component equations.

For pullbackTensorFiniteRealization_existsUnique specialize openSquarePullbackModel_existsUnique to the finite coefficient ring at exponent n+1. The constant-ring identifications and the displayed adjunction-unit section equations agree definitionally. The five remaining coherence obligations retain their named theorem statements and their docstring proof plans.

For pullbackTensorSignedTotal_existsUnique use the existing CochainComplex.Monoidal.braiding with the independent-universe monoidal, additive and coproduct-preserving sheaf tensor instances. Its ι_braiding_hom equation is the signed summand formula. Naturality of the sheafification unit and the braided sheafification functor show that the ordinary sheaf braiding swaps the displayed sheafified pure tensors. Evaluation is additive, so the integer sign passes through evaluation, giving exactly the required generator formula. For uniqueness apply isomorphism extensionality, complex-map extensionality and total-summand extensionality. Cancel the tensor-to-sheafification isomorphism and use the sheafification adjunction; presheaf and tensor-product extensionality reduce the result to equality of the prescribed generator formulas.

proof_origin.place: Tags 06YS and 07A4; componentwise restriction of the prescribed tensor model and specialization of the existing unit-normalized pullback comparison (S1 stage-3 partial proof). The signed-total proof uses the existing cochain Koszul braiding and its summand formula; sheafification naturality identifies the pure-tensor generators, and the adjunction and total-summand universal properties prove uniqueness.
